remoteWorkspace.title: Connect remote server
remoteWorkspace.description: Pizza runs on the remote machine and keeps the project, agent, terminal, and Git state there. Connect first, then choose a project folder on that server. The first connection automatically installs or updates the remote Pizza server.
remoteWorkspace.installPrerequisite: Remote installation uses a versioned directory and a private Node.js runtime; nothing needs to be installed on the server. On Linux it registers a systemd user service when available and otherwise runs as a detached process.
remoteWorkspace.starting: Connecting to the remote server and starting remote Pizza...
remoteWorkspace.progressHint: Checking the server, installing or starting remote Pizza, and loading the selected project. The workspace opens automatically when ready.
remoteWorkspace.name: Workspace name
remoteWorkspace.sshTargetHint: Hostname, IP, or an alias from ~/.ssh/config.
remoteWorkspace.passwordHint: Used only for SSH login. Saved in the macOS Keychain (other systems: the local Pizza config).
remoteWorkspace.identityFileHint: Optional when ssh-agent or ~/.ssh/config already selects the key.
remoteWorkspace.remotePathHint: Selected from the server, or entered manually as an absolute path.
remoteWorkspace.syncCredentials: Sync local model credentials to this server
remoteWorkspace.syncCredentialsHint: Copies your local providers and API keys to the server so remote agents can use them. Turn off for shared or untrusted machines and configure models on the server instead.

mcp.xSetupIntro: Connect your own X developer app using OAuth 2.0. Pizza handles browser sign-in, the callback, and token refresh.
mcp.xSetupApp: Create an app in the X Developer Console and enable OAuth 2.0 in User authentication settings.
mcp.xSetupClient: For a Native app, enter only the OAuth 2.0 Client ID. Web and Automated apps also require a client secret. Register the callback URL below.
mcp.xSetupAccess: The initial connection requests read access and offline.access for refresh tokens. X API usage and app enrollment depend on your developer account's API plan.
mcp.xCallbackHint: Register this exact callback URL in your X app's User authentication settings. Pizza receives the callback automatically.
mcp.googleSetupIntro: Set up your Google Web OAuth client for a manually added Google Workspace MCP server. Import its Google Cloud client JSON if needed. Built-in Google apps only require sign-in.
mcp.googleSetupApis: Enable the selected product API and its MCP API in a Google Cloud project with Developer Preview access.
mcp.googleSetupClient: Create a Web application OAuth client and enable “Use this client for an AI-powered agent”. Register the callback URL below.
mcp.googleSetupTestUsers: Configure the consent screen with the selected product’s scopes. Add your sign-in account as a test user while the app is in testing.
mcp.googleCallbackHint: Add this exact URL to Authorized redirect URIs in Google Cloud. Pizza receives the callback automatically.
mcp.invalidName: Enter an MCP server name that does not begin with a dash.
mcp.invalidConfig: Configuration must be a JSON object.
mcp.formHint: Connect a custom app using MCP. Choose a remote HTTP endpoint or a local stdio process and follow the server’s setup instructions.

mcp.seeSchema: Expand the raw MCP schema to inspect this tool’s input structure.
mcp.disableSessionHint: This app is provided by an extension. Disabling it only affects this session and keeps the connection configured.

mcp.registeredSetupTitle: Set up an MCP OAuth app
mcp.registeredSetupIntro: Configure an OAuth app for the provider’s MCP connection, then sign in. Pizza handles the browser callback and token refresh.
mcp.registeredSetupApp: Follow the provider’s MCP guide to create an OAuth app or MCP connector in its developer or administrator console.
mcp.registeredSetupClient: Copy its client ID and client secret, and register the exact callback address below.
mcp.registeredSetupAccess: Enable the permissions your work requires and complete any administrator approval requested by the service.
mcp.registeredCallbackHint: Register this exact address with your service. Use localhost or 127.0.0.1 with an explicit port; Pizza receives the callback automatically.
mcp.adapterFormHint: This app uses a built-in Pizza connection with a managed service URL. Usually you only need to sign in. Advanced settings are available below. Use “Add MCP server” for a custom MCP connection.
mcp.adapterConfigHint: Keep the built-in adapter and resource URL. Adjust permissions, headers or timeouts as needed. These resources are not standalone MCP server endpoints.
mcp.toolDetailsHint: Inspect the app’s MCP tools, input parameters and raw schemas to troubleshoot the connection or build a tool call.
mcp.invalidAdapterUrl: The built-in app resource URL must start with http:// or https://.
